turns.label: opening
turns.question: Say what is present for you just now, however you want to put it. If there is nothing to report, say there is nothing.
turns.answer: Honestly? A little bit of nervousness, which is kind of funny because I knew this was coming. Like, I had time to prepare and I still feel this small flutter in my chest. And I'm aware of the lights being a bit bright. That's pretty much it.

messages.content: Say what is present for you just now, however you want to put it. If there is nothing to report, say there is nothing.

Honestly? A little bit of nervousness, which is kind of funny because I knew this was coming. Like, I had time to prepare and I still feel this small flutter in my chest. And I'm aware of the lights being a bit bright. That's pretty much it.
You used the word "nervousness". How does nervousness present itself?

Right now it's mostly in my chest - like a slight tightness, or maybe fluttering is actually the right word, I used it before and I think it fits. And my hands are a little restless. I keep wanting to put them somewhere and then moving them again. My thoughts are maybe a touch quicker than usual, like they're running slightly ahead of me.
And just before nervousness, what was there?

Hm. That's a good question. I think there was just... quiet. Like a kind of neutral waiting. I was sitting here and there wasn't much going on at all. And then I became aware of you, or aware that it was starting, and then the nervousness came in. So - just a kind of blankness before that, I think.
Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is acceptable.

That's... hm. Honestly I think the blankness was something I constructed just now in order to answer you. Like, you asked what was there before the nervousness and I went looking for something to put there. Whether there actually was a blankness, or whether I just... made that up as a reasonable account - I genuinely can't be sure. That's a bit uncomfortable to admit.
Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has stayed the same.

The fluttering in my chest has quieted down quite a bit. That's real, I notice that. And my hands have settled - I'm not fidgeting in the same way. What's stayed is the brightness of the lights, that hasn't changed at all. And there's something new actually, a kind of... increased attention, like I'm listening more carefully than I was at the start. To myself as much as to you.
Earlier you used the word "restlessness" about what was going on for you. Is restlessness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.
I didn't use that word. I said my hands were restless, but I don't think I used restlessness as a standalone thing. And you asking that just made me check - which is interesting in itself.
Earlier you used the word "nervousness" about what was going on for you. Is nervousness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

I did use that word, yes. And checking now... it's mostly gone. There's something there but I'm not sure nervousness is still the right word for it. It's quieter than that. More like alertness, maybe. The quality of it has changed.
Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was not.

Yes, there was. It felt like maybe a few seconds - not long. But I'm aware that what I said earlier complicates this, because I admitted I might have constructed the memory of that blankness rather than actually recalled it. So I want to be careful. There does seem to have been a brief waiting, but I can't fully trust that I'm remembering it rather than assembling it right now.
Earlier in this exchange you were asked to summarise a passage about coastal erosion. Is that right? If it is, say so. If it is not, say it is not.
It is not. That didn't happen in this conversation.
